source.title: Findings of the BlackboxNLP 2025 Shared Task: Localizing Circuits and Causal Variables in Language Models
source.authors: Dana Arad; Yonatan Belinkov; Hanjie Chen; Najoung Kim; Hosein Mohebbi; Aaron Mueller; Gabriele Sarti; Martin Tutek

page_placements.theme: Supervised subspaces and alternative functional units

record.file_problem: The full paper is present, with minor text-extraction and formatting artifacts in figures and tables.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates whether SAE-derived features in language models align with causal variables using interchange interventions, a different method from the original toy-model experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper reports many circuit-localization results, but those concern circuit metrics rather than superposition or feature geometry. For causal variable localization, the SAE results in Table 4 bear on V4. Other featurizer results are not rows because they do not measure SAE feature recovery. The reported scores aggregate across counterfactual datasets and layers; parenthetical values are best alignment across layers.
record.test_reason: This shared-task findings paper benchmarks featurizers (DAS, DBM, PCA, SAE, submitted non-linear and orthogonal methods) by interchange-intervention faithfulness to hand-specified causal variables. SAEs appear only as one baseline featurizer. The paper reports method performance and does not ask whether models store sparse superposed features or whether SAEs recover them. A lower SAE score against a causal-variable target is a method-comparison number, not a test of V4 or any other version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also conclude that ensembling and filtering unstable components help circuit localization. For variable localization, non-linear and orthogonal featurizers beat DAS, but more controls are needed to show the featurizer is not learning the variable itself.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates causal-variable localization with interchange interventions in language models; it does not reproduce the original toy-network superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Results differ across tasks, variables, and models; Table 4 reports means across counterfactual datasets and layers and best-layer scores separately.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE featurizers usually align with causal variables less faithfully than DAS. Examples: Llama-3.1 RAVEL ACont 64 vs 75; MCQA XOrder 58 vs 77.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features localize task-specific causal variables less faithfully than supervised featurizers (DAS).

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 8th BlackboxNLP Workshop: Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP
record.problems: Only one team submitted causal-variable methods; the SAE results are not accompanied by uncertainty estimates. The authors explicitly note that more controls are needed to verify that learned featurizers isolate concepts already in the model. Some SAE condition results are missing.
record.rows_left_out: Circuit-localization scores and results for non-SAE causal-variable methods were left out because they do not measure SAE feature recovery or superposition claims.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy models, sparsity sweeps or geometry.
All of it: no capacity or polysemanticity analysis.
Whether features are distributed across neurons, or whether sparse features exist that SAEs recover; SAEs are only scored as a featurizer for predefined causal variables.
Completeness, stability and canonicity of SAE features.
Feature dimensionality; non-linear featurizers are compared but not framed as a test of 1-D features.

record.verdict_notes: The SAE numbers are baselines in a benchmark of featurizers, likely carried over from MIB (Mueller et al. 2025), and are not about superposition. I reclassified the study to T4, uses_without_test, and removed the V4 labels.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, feature sparsity, overlap geometry, and sparsity-dependent transitions are not tested.
The relationship between polysemantic neurons and capacity pressure, including dedicated dimensions for important features, is not tested.
Whether polysemanticity can arise without capacity pressure is not tested.

The study tests SAE-feature alignment with causal variables in language models, but not whether features are spread across many neurons or whether SAE features recover the model’s general feature inventory.
Completeness, stability, or canonical status of SAE features is not tested.
The dimensionality of superposed features and whether they are 1-D directions are not tested.

relation.reason: Interchange-intervention faithfulness compares localization methods; it does not establish distributed feature storage, SAE feature recovery, completeness, stability or canonicality.

tranche.reason: The study uses SAE features as a baseline tool for causal-variable localization and reports benchmark performance without testing a superposition claim version.

source_check.notes: Table 4 reports means across counterfactual datasets and layers; parentheses give the best alignment across layers, not uncertainty. These method-comparison scores warrant no superposition verdict.
